title: introduce-warmth-oracle-and-burst-fidelity-adapter
author: Ava Chen
description: Context and motivation: large tenants and bursty workloads create a repeated operational pattern: 1) cold clusters take time to reach steady KV-cache and batching efficiency, 2) ad-hoc bursts either exhaust soft quotas or produce high-per-tenant latency spikes, and 3) telemetry shows large oscillations in utilization that make predictive autoscaling noisy. This PR introduces two cooperating components — the Warmth Oracle and the Burst Fidelity Adapter — to reduce cold-start cost, stabilize autoscaling signals, and enforce tenant-level burst fidelity guarantees without hard-cap preemption. Goals: reduce cold-start tail latency for bursty tenants, smooth utilization signals used by the autoscaler, and provide per-tenant fidelity telemetry so SREs/product teams can reason about burst degradation. What this implements: - Warmth Oracle: lightweight estimator that maintains a time-decayed warmth score per cluster-pool and per-tenant fingerprint; uses recent warm-pool hit rate, KV-cache reuse ratio, and sequence-length histograms to suggest prewarm budgets and warmset priorities. It exposes two gRPC endpoints consumed by the fleet-provisioner and by the autoscaler heuristic. - Burst Fidelity Adapter (BFA): a soft enforcement layer between admission and the tenancy ledger that maps incoming burst requests to a fidelity budget. BFA prefers graceful fidelity reduction (e.g., reduce concurrency slice, slight quantization fallback, incremental batch size reduction) over outright rejections and emits fidelity-decisions as telemetry. - Telemetry and reporting: new metrics (warmth_score, fidelity_decision, fidelity_loss_estimate, tenant_fidelity_p50/p90) added to the observability-pack; a new /internal/api/v1/tenant_fidelity_report endpoint for on-demand sampling. - Autoscaler integration: the cluster autoscaler now consumes warmth_score to stabilize scale-up thresholds and to weight predicted headroom. This reduces scale oscillation for pools serving many cold-starting tenants. - Safety/fallbacks: if Warmth Oracle is unavailable, the autoscaler reverts to the previous warmset heuristic; BFA always falls back to a conservative reject path and records incidents for review. Implementation notes: - Majority of logic is in runtime/orchestration/warmth_oracle and runtime/autoscaler/adapters/burst_fidelity_adapter. - Warmth scoring is intentionally conservative: scores range 0..100 and update with exponential smoothing (alpha=0.08 default). - BFA decisions are config-driven per-tenant tier (free/standard/premium) with configurable fidelity ceilings. - Added an integration test harness that simulates multi-tenant burst patterns and validates that fidelity degradation follows expected policy. Testing and results: - Microbenchmarks: negligible CPU overhead (<= 1% median) when enabled on a standard worker node. - Integration test: simulated 100 tenant bursts; tail p95 cold-start latency improved by ~22% for affected tenants and autoscaler scale-up events reduced by ~18% in the synthetic workload. - Observability: new counters allow post-hoc attribution of fidelity loss to policy vs capacity constraints. Risks and mitigations: - Risk: tuning warmth_alpha incorrectly could under- or over-prioritize prewarming. Mitigation: default alpha conservative and surfaced in console for runtime tuning. - Risk: fidelity reductions might create user-visible regressions. Mitigation: tier-aware ceilings and runtime opt-out flags for premium tenants. Rollout plan: 1) Canary in a single non-prod region for 72h (feature flag off by default). 2) Gradual ramp to 10% of production pools, monitor fidelity_loss_estimate and p95. 3) Full enable with monitoring playbooks and rollback gates. Related: references ENG-1428 (predictive warm-pool advisor) and SUP-8812 (support ticket re: burst failures).

Implement burst fidelity adapter and decision pipeline
Wire warmth_score into autoscaler threshold logic and add feature flag
Add telemetry metrics, grafana dashboard templates, and API endpoint
Integration tests: synthetic burst harness and assertions
Docs: console feature flag UI + rollout playbook
review_comments: Diego Ruiz: Nice incremental design. Question: did you consider using the existing warmset scoring instead of a new oracle component? Can we avoid another service?

Ava Chen (author): We did an evaluation; embedding into warmset made the code paths brittle and mixed responsibilities. Oracle is a thin, low-throughput estimator with explicit fallbacks — easier to iterate and safer for rollout.
Maya Singh: Please add metrics for 'fidelity_decision_reason' (capacity|policy|oracle_hint) so we can slice later — I don't want opaque reductions.
Ava Chen: Added fidelity_decision_reason to metrics registry and to the API payloads.
Liam O'Connor: Integration test seems flakey on CI; saw a timeout on the second run. Could we reduce timer dependence?
Ava Chen: Reworked harness to use deterministic timers and mocked clock; CI runs stable now.
Diego Ruiz: Approving after minor docs nits fixed.
Maya Singh: Approval — verified dashboards and alerts during canary run.
release_notes: Added Warmth Oracle (predictive warmset advisor) and Burst Fidelity Adapter (soft tenant-level fidelity controls). New metrics: warmth_score, fidelity_decision, fidelity_loss_estimate, tenant_fidelity_p50/p90. Autoscaler now consumes warmth_score to reduce noisy scale-ups.
notes_for_ops: Feature guarded by feature flag 'warmth_oracle.enabled' and 'burst_fidelity.adapter_enabled'. Default: false. Canary plan in docs/ops/warmth-oracle-rollout.md. Monitor tenant_fidelity_p90 and autoscaler_scale_events metric; rollback if fidelity_loss_estimate > 5% sustained for 30m.
extra_context: This PR intentionally keeps the Warmth Oracle stateless from a persistence perspective — scores are in-memory with optional periodic snapshotting for debugging.
We included an example config for premium tenants to opt-out of fidelity reductions in pkg/config/feature_flags.go.
Follow-up PR planned to expose per-tenant suggested warm budgets in the console and to add an automatic tuning job for alpha.
